title: Equivariant source-decomposition cohomology for compact supports
statement:
Fix a finite field $k_0=\mathbf F_q$ of characteristic $p$, its algebraic closure $k$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, and an isomorphism $\iota:\Qlb\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf C$. For a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme $S_0$ put $S=S_0\times_{k_0}k$. Use the common-stage coefficient category $D^b_c(S,\Qlb)$ and its constructible heart [def-weil-constructible-heart]. Weil objects and equivariant morphisms are fixed pairs as in [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. Mixed upper bounds and $D_{\le w}(S_0)$ have the meanings of [def-weil-punctual-weights; def-weil-complex-weights].

Let $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ be a separated finite-type morphism of separated finite-type $k_0$-schemes, let $j_0:U_0\hookrightarrow X_0$ be an open immersion with closed complement $i_0:Z_0\hookrightarrow X_0$ [def-weil-open-immersion; def-weil-closed-immersion], and let $F$ be a constructible $\Qlb$-Weil sheaf on $X_0$. Use derived pullback [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] and the common-stage compact-support functors [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support]. Put $R^rg_{0!}G=\mathcal H^r(Rg_{0!}(G[0]))$, using standard cohomology [prop-constructible-truncations]. For every $r\in\mathbf Z$ the canonical localization arrows induce a natural sequence of constructible Weil sheaves
$$R^r(f_0j_0)_!(j_0^*F)\longrightarrow R^rf_{0!}F\longrightarrow R^r(f_0i_0)_!(i_0^*F)$$
which is exact at its middle term [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence]. The arrows are induced by the open counit and closed unit after applying $Rf_{0!}$ and the compact-support composition comparisons. They intertwine the Weil structures. This is a cohomological consequence of the underlying distinguished localization triangle in $D^b_c(Y,\Qlb)$; no triangulated structure on the fixed-pair category is assumed.

source.place: Part 1: applying cohomology to compact-support localization; old steps 4--6, sheaf half.

proof.text: First verify the functor domains. A field is Noetherian (its only ideals are $0$ and itself); thus $X_0$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. Every open subset of $X_0$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian]. For an affine open $V\subset X_0$, its inverse image under the open immersion $j_0$ is such an open subset; hence $j_0$ is quasi-compact and therefore finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-qc-open-immersion-finite-type]. The closed immersion $i_0$ is proper, in particular finite type, by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper]. Both immersions are separated by [lem-weil-pbc-separated-cancellation]. Finite-type composition [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change] and separated composition [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](e) show that $U_0,Z_0$ and the composites with $f_0$ have the required separated finite-type structure maps. Their geometric fibres have the same properties by [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change]. These are precisely the schemes and maps used below.

source.place: Part 1: verification of the finite-type domains of the localization triangle and compact-support functors.

proof.text: Put $K=F[0]$ in the underlying common-stage category $D^b_c(X,\Qlb)$. Apply [lem-a1-constructible-pullback-t-exact] to the geometric immersions $j$ and $i$: their derived pullbacks preserve the constructible hearts, so $j^*K=(j^*F)[0]$ and $i^*K=(i^*F)[0]$, with the natural heart-inclusion identifications. Their Weil structures are the pullback structures supplied by [prop-weil-operations]. Thus the sheaves used to define the two outer higher images are precisely the restrictions in the statement, without adding any weight hypothesis.

source.place: Part 1, sheaf form: localization, compact-support composition, and cohomology of the underlying distinguished triangle.

proof.text: Use [prop-sf-open-closed-triangle-all-stages] at $\Lambda=\Qlb$ and this $K$. It gives the functorial distinguished triangle $j_!j^*K\xrightarrow{\epsilon_K}K\xrightarrow{\eta_K}i_*i^*K\longrightarrow j_!j^*K[1]$ in $D^b_c(X,\Qlb)$. Its first two arrows are the open counit and closed unit. All three arrows are equivariant since the immersions are defined over $k_0$ and $K$ carries its given Weil structure. This is a triangle in the underlying category.

source.place: Part 1, sheaf form: localization, compact-support composition, and cohomology of the underlying distinguished triangle.

proof.text: The compact-support functor is exact on this bounded constructible domain and lifts to Weil pairs by [prop-weil-operations]. Apply its underlying exact functor to the preceding triangle. By clause (3) of [prop-functor-package], compact-support composition and proper/ordinary coincidence for the closed immersion identify the result with a distinguished triangle $A\xrightarrow{a}B\xrightarrow{b}C\longrightarrow A[1]$, where $A=R(fj)_!j^*K$, $B=Rf_!K$, and $C=R(fi)_!i^*K$. Explicitly, if $c_j:A\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_!j_!j^*K$ and $c_i:C\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_!i_*i^*K$ are those comparisons, then $a=Rf_!(\epsilon_K)c_j$ and $b=c_i^{-1}Rf_!(\eta_K)$. The comparisons are natural and equivariant by [prop-weil-operations], so these are the specified canonical equivariant arrows. All three objects lie in $D^b_c(Y,\Qlb)$, the field-coefficient domain of the package.

source.place: Part 1, sheaf form: localization, compact-support composition, and cohomology of the underlying distinguished triangle.

proof.text: By [prop-constructible-truncations], the common-stage category on $Y$ has its standard bounded t-structure and heart-valued functors $\mathcal H^r$. Apply clause (5) of [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles] to the underlying triangle of Step 4. For every integer $r$ its long exact sequence is exact at $\mathcal H^r(B)$ in the constructible heart. Using Step 2, its same-degree segment is $R^r(f_0j_0)_!(j_0^*F)\xrightarrow{\mathcal H^r(a)}R^rf_{0!}F\xrightarrow{\mathcal H^r(b)}R^r(f_0i_0)_!(i_0^*F)$. In particular this asserts equality of the image and kernel of these actual canonical maps, rather than only the existence of some maps between isomorphic objects.

source.place: Part 1, sheaf form: localization, compact-support composition, and cohomology of the underlying distinguished triangle.

proof.text: The functor on cohomology Weil pairs is [lem-pod-fixed-pair-truncation-cohomology]. For clarity write $P=Lg_Y^*$, $c_D:P\mathcal H^r(D)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal H^r(PD)$, and $\theta_D^r=\mathcal H^r(\theta_D)c_D$. For either equivariant arrow $u:D\to E$ of Step 4, naturality of $c$ and $u\theta_D=\theta_E P(u)$ give $\mathcal H^r(u)\theta_D^r=\mathcal H^r(\theta_E)\mathcal H^r(Pu)c_D=\theta_E^r P(\mathcal H^r(u))$. Thus both maps of Step 5 are morphisms of the stated constructible Weil sheaves. Naturality in $F$ follows by applying the same cohomology functor to the functorial localization arrows and their natural composition comparisons in Steps 3--4.

source.place: Part 1, sheaf form: localization, compact-support composition, and cohomology of the underlying distinguished triangle.

proof.text: Exactness also holds in the Weil heart. Indeed $P$ and its inverse preserve the heart and are exact there: use the automorphism equivalence of [lem-sf-automorphism-constructible-stage-equivalence], the automorphism/truncation compatibility of [prop-constructible-truncations], and the short-exact-sequence/triangle criterion of [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles]. Here is the elementary universal-property argument for forgetting pairs [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. If $u:D\to E$ is equivariant and $k:M\to D$ is its underlying kernel, $Pk$ is a kernel of $Pu$; the square with the two invertible Weil structures therefore induces a unique isomorphism $\theta_M:PM\to M$ with $k\theta_M=\theta_D Pk$. Any equivariant map into $D$ killed by $u$ factors uniquely through $k$, and its factor is equivariant by cancellation of the monomorphism $k$. Dually the underlying cokernel carries a unique invertible Weil structure and has the cokernel universal property for pairs. Thus kernels, cokernels, and consequently images are computed on the underlying heart; its image--kernel equality from Step 5 is the same equality in the Weil heart. This is exactly middle exactness in [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence]. The argument uses only triangles of the underlying coefficient category.

Then the bounded t-structure of prop-constructible-truncations and clause (5) of lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles for every integer r, which stand in for lem-sp-long-exact-of-triangle. Equivariance comes from lem-pod-fixed-pair-truncation-cohomology, and Step 7 is an elementary kernel/cokernel argument in the pair category; I checked the theta_M construction and the mono cancellation. Step 1's eight geometric checks are Mathlib leaves that say what the step uses. Step 2: t-exactness gives j^*(F[0]) = (j^*F)[0]. Small cases (Z or U empty, F = 0, A^1 with G_m, negative r, Jordan-block Frobenius) are all exact at the middle. The statement matches what the sibling lem-zl-exact-middle-weight-bound needs. Two minor glosses, not counted as faults: equivariance of Ri_! = Ri_* (trivial compactification), and the two forms of H^i (they agree by shift compatibility).
